nodes.label: installedPack Jar Exclusions
nodes.rationale: build.gradle excludes AmbientSounds, CreativeCore, sound-physics-remastered and PresenceFootsteps jars when building installedPack from client-mods.

nodes.label: AmbientSounds
nodes.rationale: Supplies streamed environmental recordings selected from world context (source commit c9a07218c5581171adf4b0a9575f5a506eb4fd27, LGPL-3.0).

nodes.label: Presence Footsteps
nodes.rationale: Supplies positional material recordings for the stride engine (source commit 975736d208e0fd7edb20b49eb57ef2c4f4cafda4, MIT).

nodes.label: Sound Physics Remastered
nodes.rationale: Supplies OpenAL EFX reverberation, occlusion, absorption and reflected directionality; ambient.* events are skipped to avoid spending reflection rays on non-positional beds (source commit ce6c71b8a5fcffc50e75d0407c9c516b0bfca515, GPL-3.0).

nodes.label: Private Audio Physics Namespace
nodes.rationale: Ark uses dev.nez.arksurvivalreturns.client.audio.physics for replacement classes and its .mixin subpackage for mixins, with 39 private-package entries and zero old-package entries in the packaged jar.

nodes.label: Unified Audio Engine
nodes.rationale: One client-only runtime embeds three audio systems so the standalone source mods must not be installed alongside Ark; dedicated servers can load the jar without client audio classes.

nodes.label: Audio Loader Conflict Audit (DeepSeek V4.1)
nodes.rationale: Document-only audit produced by the external API model alias deepseek-flash using parent-supplied evidence; the worker had no direct checkout access and did not rerun commands.

nodes.label: Audio Resource-Pack API (catalog.json)
nodes.rationale: Override audio/catalog.json in a resource pack to change footsteps, soundTypes and ambience without recompiling; omitted conditions are wildcards and long ambience files should declare stream:true.

nodes.label: Commit 31d5225 Sound Physics Loader Conflict Fix
nodes.norm_label: commit 31d5225 sound physics loader conflict fix
nodes.rationale: Removes package/classloader overlap with the standalone Sound Physics Remastered jar while keeping Ark's integrated implementation; the audit returned PASS limited to parent-supplied evidence, with no independent runtime test.

nodes.label: NaturalPopulations Budget
nodes.rationale: Owns an independent spawn budget that does not compete for the vanilla animal cap; the resolution explicitly kept this for finding 2.

nodes.label: Spawn and Biome Rules Inspection 2026-09-19
nodes.rationale: Symptom: walking the Overworld finds no Ark creatures; the growing emptiness is explained by an ordered chain of defects that the headless tests never execute.

nodes.label: Defect: Chunk-Gen Spawns Despawn at Frontier
nodes.norm_label: defect: chunk-gen spawns despawn at frontier
nodes.rationale: removeWhenFarAway always returns true and persistence is set only for eggs and commands, so chunk-generation creatures placed at simulation distance would vanish within seconds unless persistence is set.

nodes.label: Defect: Footprint Y Equals Highest Column
nodes.norm_label: defect: footprint y equals highest column
nodes.rationale: The predicate requires the spawn Y to equal the highest block of a multi-column footprint while ON_GROUND supplies that column's heightmap Y, so any neighbor one block taller rejects the spawn; flat game-test pads never expose this.

nodes.label: Spawn Placement Resolution (current build)
nodes.rationale: canSpawn resolves the server world through world.getLevel(), natural wildlife no longer despawns, water realms register as WATER_CREATURE, groundFits accepts bounded slopes and clearForBody checks a feet slab plus headroom while ignoring leaves.

nodes.label: Defect: Population Director Removed
nodes.rationale: All 41 species register as CREATURE sharing vanilla cap 10 with livestock, and the old director's independent budget was deleted while the live config still documents it, so the periodic spawner almost never adds Ark mobs.

nodes.label: Defect: Spawns Rejected on WorldGenRegion
nodes.rationale: canSpawn and canSpawnWater require instanceof ServerLevel, but chunk generation calls with a WorldGenRegion, so every Ark species is forbidden at the only phase where MobCategory.CREATURE fills the world.

nodes.label: Defect: Water Species on Wrong Spawn Category
nodes.norm_label: defect: water species on wrong spawn category
nodes.rationale: Oceans and rivers have biome modifiers but no sharks or plesiosaurs appear because CREATURE chunk gen samples ground columns while the WATER_CREATURE passes never see these types.

nodes.label: Population Director
nodes.rationale: Checks every 5 seconds targeting 3 distinct wild groups within 96 blocks of each active player, adds at most 2 groups per dimension per check, samples 32-80 blocks away in already loaded entity-ticking chunks and never requests chunks.

nodes.label: Disposable Codex worktree
nodes.rationale: Worker runs read-only and returns a Git patch because nested third-party Codex sessions cannot execute commands under the Windows sandbox on this host.

nodes.label: DeepSeek delegation trigger sentence
nodes.rationale: Primary agent must construct the task, review the worker commit independently, and report token counts; never claim an OpenAI subagent as the DeepSeek worker.

nodes.label: WildlifeGoal
nodes.rationale: Mod-side goal attached to registered entities that drives the wildlife mind and registers server event listeners for noise.

nodes.label: Phantom Circle/Swoop Reuse
nodes.rationale: Adapt PhantomCircleAroundAnchorGoal, PhantomAttackStrategyGoal, PhantomSweepAttackGoal and PhantomMoveControl movement patterns into the existing creature hierarchy rather than subclassing the hostile mob; whole-body collision lookahead is required because scaled birds are much larger.

nodes.label: Flying Habitats Proposal
nodes.rationale: Approved 10 September 2026 including perching, implemented 11 September; it replaces the flyers' land routines without requiring ARK's behavior trees to execute inside Minecraft.

nodes.label: Persistent Flying Colony Habitat
nodes.rationale: A persistent habitat is the shared home of 3-4 birds with several small nests and one map symbol; a server-confirmed egg-taking event is the only permission to attack a player, and new nests plus the complete bird group must succeed together or be rolled back.

nodes.label: Egg-Taking Contract
nodes.rationale: Mark the responsible player only after the server confirms the egg was taken; track that player's UUID and expiry, notify only living members of that habitat, and never let an inventory scan continuously renew aggression.

nodes.label: Flyer Flight State Machine
nodes.rationale: Two main flight behaviors (ordinary roaming and egg defense) plus explicit return/recovery phases so failure has a safe outcome; the stock Phantom attack strategy must be changed to preserve a habitat leash.

nodes.label: Xaero Nest Glyph
nodes.rationale: One small nest-and-egg glyph at the saved habitat center with a separate nests toggle; drawn as a compact pixel pattern through the existing bridge so no renderer or texture dependency is added, and only discovered habitats are sent.

nodes.label: Six-stage creature conversion pipeline
nodes.rationale: Preserves original ARK skeletons and clips bound to exact bone names; extraction never writes to the Steam game directory and stops instead of guessing package offsets.

nodes.label: UModel / UE Viewer executable
nodes.rationale: Keep the executable hash with regenerated extraction manifests because changing extractor builds can change coordinate or scale behavior; the game files are read only.

nodes.label: Delivered build requirements lock
nodes.rationale: Versions used for the delivered builds on Python 3.12.10, Windows x64.

nodes.label: Preview requirements (Numba)
nodes.rationale: Optional numba pin enables correct hidden-surface previews for dense cuboid models.

nodes.label: UE Viewer MIT License
nodes.rationale: MIT License, Copyright 2022 Konstantin Nosov; preserved as upstream license text.

nodes.label: Standardized change log policy
nodes.rationale: CHANGELOG.md is the canonical player-facing patch history; never describe a build check as visual verification and never invent earlier releases.

nodes.label: GitHub backup directive
nodes.rationale: Routine add/commit/push after every completed main execution is authorized, but force-push and secrets, saves or build outputs are never allowed.

nodes.label: Standardized patch methodology
nodes.rationale: A new chat is opened per patch theme: concept proposal with multiplayer performance impact first, then user direction, then execution, then tuning.

nodes.label: Wildlife Behavior Research and Implemented Model
nodes.community_name: Wildlife Behavior Research and Implemented Model
nodes.norm_label: wildlife behavior research and implemented model
nodes.rationale: Immersion needs understandable causes, so the model separates perception, remembered information, decisions, navigation and presentation; it recreates ARK concepts in Java with its own rules instead of executing Unreal Blueprints.

nodes.label: Nighttime Patch Proposal
nodes.community_name: Wildlife Behavior Research and Implemented Model
nodes.rationale: Prepared 9 September 2026 as a proposal for feedback, not implemented; the recommended experience is a quieter daytime wilderness with sleeping animals and nights of visible predator activity.

nodes.label: Implemented Behavior Contract
nodes.community_name: Wildlife Behavior Research and Implemented Model
nodes.rationale: Perception to last-known position to needs to WildlifeMind decision to navigation/presentation, with states Roam, Forage, Seek water, Drink, Rest, Alert, Investigate, Threaten, Hunt, Defend, Flee, Return home and Feed.

nodes.label: Bounded Simulation Limits
nodes.community_name: Wildlife Behavior Research and Implemented Model
nodes.rationale: Sensing evaluates at most 24 entities, noise history caps at 64 entries per dimension, and there is no offscreen simulation, unlimited path search, forced chunk loading or terrain regeneration.

nodes.label: Collection Day and Night Routines
nodes.community_name: Wildlife Behavior Research and Implemented Model
nodes.rationale: Every non-flying species keeps the shared WildlifeMind; nighttime carnivore hunger uses the configured multiplier, nocturnal species never enter SLEEP because water species have no authored sleep pose, and cold routines stay gradual and individually staggered.

nodes.label: Existing Behavior Family Reuse
nodes.community_name: Wildlife Behavior Research and Implemented Model
nodes.rationale: New creatures reuse existing family profiles (Allosaurus uses the Raptor pack profile) so territory, shared hunger, loaded-chunk navigation budgets, replenishment and nighttime routines stay unchanged; more species grow the selection pool, not the simultaneous population limit.

nodes.label: Daytime Carnivore Sleep and Roaming
nodes.community_name: Wildlife Behavior Research and Implemented Model
nodes.rationale: Unthreatened carnivores spend roughly 70% of routine time sleeping and 30% slowly roaming near home with individual variation; a distant passerby must not keep them awake indefinitely.

nodes.label: Gradual Dusk and Dawn Transitions
nodes.community_name: Wildlife Behavior Research and Implemented Model
nodes.rationale: Animals settle or wake across about 20-30 seconds instead of switching together; dawn never forces sleep during damage, pursuit or immediate danger, and local shade and rain affect perception rather than turning daytime nocturnal.

nodes.label: Night Vision for Active Hunters
nodes.community_name: Wildlife Behavior Research and Implemented Model
nodes.rationale: Hunters retain daytime sight distance at night, replacing the current 30% darkness penalty for those profiles; rain, crouching, facing and cover still matter.

nodes.label: 2x Nighttime Hunger Growth
nodes.community_name: Wildlife Behavior Research and Implemented Model
nodes.rationale: Start with 2x nighttime hunger growth keeping the 0.4 hunt threshold; a predator returns from 0.05 satiety to the threshold in about 3.5 minutes at 20 TPS, versus seven minutes at the current rate.

nodes.label: Red Emissive Eyes at Night
nodes.community_name: Wildlife Behavior Research and Implemented Model
nodes.rationale: Awake carnivores have red emissive eyes from dusk to dawn using depth-tested eye-only geometry; dynamic red lights are skipped initially because emissive eyes provide the warning without another lighting dependency.

nodes.label: Scheduled Sleep vs Fatigue Rest
nodes.community_name: Wildlife Behavior Research and Implemented Model
nodes.rationale: Add a clear distinction between scheduled sleep and brief fatigue rest; fatigue reaching zero must not immediately end a scheduled sleep period, and torpor animations must not silently stand in for natural sleep.

nodes.label: DangerMapSync Entitlement
nodes.community_name: Taming, Torpor and Riding Debugging Guide
nodes.rationale: Server-to-client packet synchronizes permission and saved difficulty origin/width; the future taming system can grant entitlement via DangerMapSync.setUnlocked, and there is no client-to-server unlock message.

nodes.label: /arktaming Operator Commands
nodes.community_name: Taming, Torpor and Riding Debugging Guide
nodes.rationale: inspect, torpor, hunger, reset, mount, roster and log all require gamemaster permission; roster fails loudly if a creature, food tag or seat is missing.

nodes.label: CompanionGoal (FOLLOW/STAY/WANDER)
nodes.community_name: Taming, Torpor and Riding Debugging Guide
nodes.rationale: A companion never teleports and never loads a chunk: an absent, unreachable or other-dimensional owner leaves it holding position until the owner returns.

nodes.label: CreatureAnimationBridge
nodes.community_name: Taming, Torpor and Riding Debugging Guide
nodes.rationale: sedationClip is asked first so a restricted phase always wins over locomotion and attack; it maps COLLAPSING, TORPID feeding, unconscious loop and wake clips and returns null when the caller should choose its ordinary clip.

nodes.label: CreatureEntity Riding and Tame State
nodes.community_name: Taming, Torpor and Riding Debugging Guide
nodes.rationale: Owns seat attachment, positionRider, controlling-passenger exposure and ridden input; getRiddenInput reads ServerPlayer.getLastClientInput on the server because a remote player's xxa/zza are never filled server-side.

nodes.label: CreatureInventory
nodes.community_name: Taming, Torpor and Riding Debugging Guide
nodes.rationale: Nine food/storage slots written to the entity's TamingInventory child tag, synced via the open menu only; shift-click paths mirror the vanilla horse menu and death drops contents exactly once.

nodes.label: CreatureEntity.strike Hit-Frame Timing
nodes.community_name: Taming, Torpor and Riding Debugging Guide
nodes.rationale: Melee damage is tied to the attack clip: the hit is scheduled for the authored clip length times combat.hitFrameFraction and revalidates range and sight, so a target that steps away makes the swing whiff.

nodes.label: TamingService
nodes.community_name: Taming, Torpor and Riding Debugging Guide
nodes.rationale: Validates feeding in order (taming switch, eligibility, tamed, wrong state, claim, food tag, appetite, cooldown) and only then consumes food; ownership goes to the claimant, never the last feeder, and inventory autoConsume shares the same advance path.

nodes.label: TamingState Attachment
nodes.community_name: Taming, Torpor and Riding Debugging Guide
nodes.rationale: Holds taming progress, claimant, owner, feeding appetite, meals and the attempt clock; the feeding truce is deliberately not persisted or synced and resets on every load.

nodes.label: ARK Community Wiki (reference)
nodes.community_name: Taming, Torpor and Riding Debugging Guide

nodes.label: Tranquilizer Arrow
nodes.community_name: Taming, Torpor and Riding Debugging Guide
nodes.rationale: Narcoberry consumption is the basic exposure and a craftable tranquilizer arrow is the survival delivery method for wild creatures; ordinary punches and all weapons must not silently become tranquilizers.

nodes.label: Taming, Torpor and Riding Debugging Guide
nodes.community_name: Taming, Torpor and Riding Debugging Guide
nodes.norm_label: taming, torpor and riding debugging guide
nodes.rationale: Everything except rendered seat and animation review can be reproduced headlessly with game tests and operator commands because the user performs interactive client testing.

nodes.label: Taming Patch Proposal
nodes.community_name: Taming, Torpor and Riding Debugging Guide
nodes.rationale: Prepared 2026-09-13 and implemented on 2026-09-16; the counts and species list describe the proposal as written when the roster was 19 species, so it is a design record rather than current documentation.

nodes.label: Rider Seat Manifest
nodes.community_name: Taming, Torpor and Riding Debugging Guide
nodes.rationale: Seats are measured from each runtime model's back bone, rotated by the 180 degrees the renderer applies; 0 of 41 seats fall outside their own mesh, but hitbox containment is not proven for the 24 meshes that are not normalised.

nodes.label: Taming Roster and Rider Seats
nodes.community_name: Taming, Torpor and Riding Debugging Guide
nodes.rationale: Generated by tools/build_taming_roster.py from CreatureProfileRegistry, the seat manifest and the animation matrix; do not edit by hand, change the profile table or models and rerun the tool.

nodes.label: Imported Torpor Clips
nodes.community_name: Taming, Torpor and Riding Debugging Guide
nodes.rationale: Species without a source torpor sequence fall back to their authored standing sleep pose, and the animation bridge reports which clip it selected so a missing asset can never silently look like a broken controller.

nodes.label: Weight and Logistics System
nodes.community_name: Taming, Torpor and Riding Debugging Guide
nodes.rationale: Mass creates logistics, not inventory punishment: slots remain organization capacity while mass controls mobility, and specialist reductions apply exactly once with no recursive multiplication through nested containers; changes are computed on inventory mutation, never by scanning every slot every tick.

nodes.label: Familiarity System (0-100)
nodes.community_name: Taming, Torpor and Riding Debugging Guide
nodes.rationale: Post-taming care distinct from progress and sedation with per-category cooldowns, no offline decay and no ownership loss; bonuses stay modest to avoid compounding wild level scaling, and health/damage/level multipliers are avoided until mounted combat is balanced.

nodes.label: Predator Food-Offering Prototype
nodes.community_name: Taming, Torpor and Riding Debugging Guide
nodes.rationale: An optional Velociraptor experiment: a hungry animal investigates a placed offering only with a reachable path, tolerates the provider briefly, and needs repeat windows plus a final close feed; it is not a silent replacement of carnivore knockout taming.

nodes.label: Knockout Taming Loop
nodes.community_name: Taming, Torpor and Riding Debugging Guide
nodes.rationale: Inspect, deliver torpor, collapse, unlock the wild inventory, deposit suitable food and narcoberries, periodic eating, successful wake-up, hearts and tame controls; completion takes precedence over a torpor-zero tie and death takes precedence over completion.

nodes.label: Passive Feeding Taming
nodes.community_name: Taming, Torpor and Riding Debugging Guide
nodes.rationale: Observe, approach with eligible food, feed once, wait for appetite, repeat to ownership; sprinting into the animal, attacking it or a real predator threat interrupts feeding, and a real attack removes only a bounded portion of progress.

nodes.label: Torpor Status Effect
nodes.community_name: Taming, Torpor and Riding Debugging Guide
nodes.rationale: Maintain an authoritative current/max torpor meter separately from effect duration: a lingering dose builds torpor while the meter decides collapse, and effect expiration alone must not force an unconscious animal to stand up.

nodes.label: Model Normalisation Seating Defect
nodes.community_name: Taming, Torpor and Riding Debugging Guide
nodes.rationale: 24 of 41 meshes are not normalised to their entity origin, so seat height is clamped into the registered hitbox; it is a pre-existing asset pipeline limitation (declared visible_bounds are inaccurate in several projects), not a taming rule.

nodes.label: Per-Meal Taming Progress
nodes.community_name: Taming, Torpor and Riding Debugging Guide
nodes.rationale: Progress per meal is derived, not configured twice: a tame needs ceil(targetDuration / 20 s) meals so one baseline meal is 100/meals percent; a full torpor bar keeps a creature unconscious about 170 seconds, so longer tames need narcoberry topping up.

nodes.label: Taming, Torpor and Riding System
nodes.community_name: Taming, Torpor and Riding Debugging Guide
nodes.rationale: Every one of the 41 creatures can be tamed and ridden; torpor has size-dependent ceilings of 60/150/350/700 with a ten second recovery delay and 0.5% recovery per second, and progress comes from meals rather than waiting.

nodes.label: NestBlock.disturb
nodes.rationale: Alerts the nearby bird whose nestPosition() is the disturbed nest; neither proximity nor another player's inventory grants attack authority.

nodes.label: Ark Repository Conventions (AGENTS.md)
nodes.rationale: Use the Gradle wrapper, runData after data provider changes, commit generated resources and never hand-edit them, run build and runGameTestServer for gameplay changes, never launch runClient, keep common/server code free of client imports, and spawning must never force chunk loads.

nodes.label: Flying Ecosystem Implementation
nodes.rationale: The original colony design was replaced by vanilla spawning plus one local nest per bird; the difficulty map, danger gating and level scaling are unchanged.

nodes.label: Land Ecosystem Implementation
nodes.rationale: Implemented 2026-09-14 from the approved proposal; the current runtime has nineteen species, seventeen of them land creatures.

nodes.label: Land Ecosystem Proposal
nodes.rationale: Design and symbol assets prepared 2026-09-11; all distances are proposed tuning defaults and the values below are not measured results.

nodes.label: Gameplay Test Coverage
nodes.rationale: Covers save persistence, difficulty recurrence and area shares, spawn eligibility, actual population spawning, behavior decisions, real predator/prey combat and movement calibration within 4% of configured targets.

nodes.label: Verification Baseline 2026-09-07
nodes.rationale: Historical baseline: 18 JUnit tests and all eight headless GameTests passed on NeoForge 26.2.0.11-beta and GeckoLib 5.5.3; current flying behavior is documented in the Flying Ecosystem page.

nodes.label: Bounded Collision Lookahead
nodes.rationale: Overlapping body-sized segments along the route bounded to 64, after checking all involved chunks are loaded; no 3D pathfinder, boid simulation or need searches run for flyers.

nodes.label: Flyer Egg Collection and Defense
nodes.rationale: One damage attempt per swoop with melee range and line of sight required; defense expires after 600 ticks, 60 ticks without visible contact, an invalid player or the 64-block horizontal leash, and transient defense clears on reload.

nodes.label: One Local Nest per Bird
nodes.rationale: A natural flyer claims a single nest near where it spawned; no colony record, member list or map marker is saved, and a flyer that never finds a valid local site simply keeps flying with no nest.

nodes.label: Forced One-Shot Animation Clips
nodes.rationale: Triggered landing, takeoff, pull-out, warning and attack clips are forced to play once because several imported source montages are flagged to loop and would otherwise override the perched or locomotion pose forever.

nodes.label: Shared Group Hunger Clock
nodes.rationale: Each active habitat advances one hunger clock at most once per second; a kill satisfies the group once, grazing credit depends on the fraction of reserved members foraging, and offline time does not accumulate hunger updates.

nodes.label: Land Habitat Map Markers
nodes.rationale: One stable home marker per discovered habitat, discovered per player within 96 horizontal and 64 vertical blocks, up to the nearest 128; the symbol represents the saved home, never a live creature tracker.

nodes.label: Land Group Coordinator
nodes.rationale: One coordinator advances each active group's hunger once for elapsed simulated ticks (five member callbacks must not advance it five times); inactive groups freeze and there is no offscreen catch-up.

nodes.label: Habitat Lifecycle and Save Migration
nodes.rationale: UUID reservations are the authority for occupancy because missing from a nearby query across chunks does not mean dead; unload pauses work, permanent removal releases a reservation once after a cooldown, and water loss triggers bounded relocation that keeps the habitat ID.

nodes.label: Land Habitat Leaf and Fang Glyphs
nodes.norm_label: land habitat leaf and fang glyphs
nodes.rationale: Two 9x9 two-color vector assets extend the nest glyph style; distinct silhouettes stay useful when colors are hard to distinguish, and they are prepared design assets not wired into the runtime by the proposal.

nodes.label: Persistent Land Habitat
nodes.rationale: Each natural group has one dry home coordinate near usable surface water, one shared hunger value and one routine/destination; habitat identity owns the group's lifecycle so a herd walking away does not drag its map marker along.

nodes.label: Shared Group Satiation
nodes.rationale: One confirmed non-player kill feeds a group once, deduplicated by victim UUID so simultaneous hits cannot multiply the reward; nearby unrelated packs receive no food, and grazing credit depends on the fraction of members actually foraging.

nodes.label: Water Qualification Detector
nodes.rationale: Use a reusable index of water samples with fixed work budgets and an explicit unknown answer when sampling is unfinished or chunks are unloaded; unknown must not become a permanent dry classification, and sparse sampling may miss a thin river.

nodes.label: Water Distance Weight Function
nodes.rationale: waterWeight is 1 inside the preferred distance, declines linearly to 0 at the exclusion distance, and a rejected candidate creates neither a natural group nor a habitat/marker; zero must be rejected before minimum-weight rounding clamps positive weights to one.

nodes.label: Occupancy Replacement Cooldown
nodes.rationale: Permanent member removal opens a slot after 12,000 ticks (ten minutes) by default while chunk unloading keeps the reservation; vacant habitats still count toward the local group target so leaving and returning cannot immediately reroll them.

nodes.label: Valid Water Sample Rule
nodes.rationale: Exposed ordinary water with at least eight connected cells in a 4x4 window and a connected 2x2 patch; waterlogged blocks, isolated pools, covered water and missing chunks do not qualify, and sparse sampling may miss extremely narrow rivers.

nodes.label: Land Ecosystem Work Bounds
nodes.rationale: At most 256 reserved block/height probes per dimension tick (background discovery at most half), queue max 256 chunks, cache 2048 chunk entries, eight requests per 100 ticks; these bound work but are not measured FPS/MSPT guarantees.

nodes.label: WildlifeMind Decision Model
nodes.rationale: Decision layer driven by needs, confidence, warning time and home range; runs twice per second per animal, staggered by entity ID.

nodes.label: LandWildlife.coldHydration
nodes.rationale: Snow cover, powder snow or ice over water satisfies cold-species hydration; bare packed ice is never a drink source, ice is never broken, and snow over valid browse ground abstracts foraging without terrain damage.

nodes.label: Species.realm()
nodes.rationale: Derived from the profile so a species cannot silently lose its realm: LandFamily.AQUATIC means water, a swim clip set means amphibious, a flight policy means air.

nodes.label: scripts/workflow.py Rebuild Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Re-extracts the ten source projects from the repository root; --reuse-exports supports offline builds from preserved source exports.

nodes.label: Acrocanthosaurus Rig
nodes.rationale: Retains native bind rotations to preserve anisotropic bone scaling; runtime ID is acrocanthosaurus despite the local folder spelling Acrochantosaur.

nodes.label: Ceratosaurus Native Bind Rotations
nodes.rationale: Ceratosaurus and Acrocanthosaurus retain native bind rotations; existing baked-axis models keep their established convention.

nodes.label: Ten New Creature Roster
nodes.rationale: Spinosaurus, Parasaur, Ceratosaurus, Dilophosaur, Acrocanthosaurus, Allosaurus, Ankylosaurus, Carnotaurus, Pegomastax and Lystrosaurus join the existing nine; the playable mod imports seven clips per new creature.

nodes.label: Six Cold Species
nodes.rationale: Direwolf, Mammoth, Megalocerus, Megapithecus, Sabertooth and Unicorn are source-only and still need entity registration, attributes, importer entries, spawn profiles, loot and localization.

nodes.label: Cold Sweat (temperature mod)
nodes.rationale: Published compatibility list does not include Minecraft 26.2; no working install may be promised and a mismatched JAR must not be fetched.

nodes.label: Collection Ecosystem (ice, flying, aquatic, swamp)
nodes.rationale: The 22 source-only Collection projects are registered runtime species reporting status, group settings, a saved home and day/night routines through the same decision model the original nineteen use.

nodes.label: Collection Group Settings Table
nodes.rationale: Water, swamp and cold groups are intentionally small because a pool or shoreline home is a scarce resource; most species are solitary and only Sarco, the cold grazers and warm pack hunters share a home.

nodes.label: Snow Biome Proposal
nodes.rationale: Proposal for feedback dated 2026-09-14; no cold species have been registered or deployed by this document, and all values are starting design values rather than biological claims.

nodes.label: 41-Species Spawn Roster
nodes.rationale: Group sizes, base weights, base HP, base damage and preferred habitats for every registered species; natural spawns allow at most 24 Ark creatures within 96 blocks and require 24 blocks between solitary creatures of the same species.

nodes.label: Realm System (WATER/AMPHIBIOUS/LAND/AIR)
nodes.rationale: A species belongs to one realm that decides where it lives, how it moves and where it spawns; spawning goes through the vanilla spawner via per-species biome tags and no habitat record is saved.

nodes.label: Cold Site Profiles
nodes.rationale: Valley grove, ridge shelter and secluded clearing reuse the land habitat model; an exposed-water requirement for every habitat would make frozen areas unreliable, so cold habitats accept snow-supported hydration as a species policy.

nodes.label: Frozen-Water Hydration Policy
nodes.rationale: A frozen river counts only if a bounded check confirms water beneath a shallow ice layer; arbitrary packed-ice structures are never a drink source and cold-adapted creatures satisfy thirst slowly at a safe snow patch instead.

nodes.label: Megapithecus Guardian Role
nodes.rationale: ARK introduced Megapithecus as a boss in a snowy mountain arena, so a rare avoidable territorial guardian works with an open ecosystem; no minions, throwing rocks or arena generation in the first implementation.

nodes.label: Rare Habitat Spacing (512 blocks)
nodes.rationale: Rare habitats start at least 512 blocks from the same special species' other saved habitat using the saved spatial index; this is a rarity rule, not a global singleton or an instruction to load remote chunks.

nodes.label: Gradle runData/build/runGameTestServer release gate
nodes.rationale: CI regenerates data, builds the mod and runs headless GameTests on pushes and pull requests; it is the documented release gate.

nodes.label: Anatomy-Driven Creature Textures patch
nodes.rationale: Stable per-UUID variant keeps creature appearance across saves and consistent for every client.

nodes.label: Apex Encounters and Night Eyes patch
nodes.norm_label: apex encounters and night eyes patch
nodes.rationale: Biome tag used as a spawn weight instead of a hard gate; giant placement checks a feet slab plus headroom so an apex can stand under a canopy.

nodes.label: Hit-Frame Combat and Companion Orders patch
nodes.norm_label: hit-frame combat and companion orders patch
nodes.rationale: Damage lands on the authored hit frame of each attack clip; companion orders deliberately have no teleport.

nodes.label: Natural spawning rework
nodes.rationale: Titanosaur and Giganotosaurus are budget-only because the vanilla world-generation spawner crashes when a body is wider than one chunk.

nodes.label: Taming, Torpor and Riding patch
nodes.rationale: Seats derive from each creature's own back bone; the vanilla horse screen is reused; torpor, taming and riding share one server-authoritative implementation.

nodes.label: Theme Alignment patch
nodes.rationale: The mod is a prehistoric survival experience, so fantasy and alternate-dimension content no longer competes with hunting and reading terrain.

nodes.label: Unified Spatial Audio patch
nodes.rationale: Sound Physics Remastered EFX merged into the Ark runtime, ported directly to NeoForge without a second mod container; license set to GPL-3.0-only.

nodes.label: Vanilla Spawning patch
nodes.rationale: The water-adjacent habitat spawn gate made the world feel sparse; vanilla mob caps and despawn now own density.

nodes.label: 41-creature runtime roster
nodes.rationale: All 41 creature projects are registered by the mod and appear naturally in the Overworld; spawn values come from Species.java and group config is size / weight.

nodes.label: prepareDevRuntime Gradle Task
nodes.community_name: Optional Client Pack and Difficulty Map
nodes.rationale: Applies distance settings to ignored run/options.txt and run/server.properties, preserving other keys and reapplying explicit dev values if those keys change; no EULA acceptance is written.

nodes.label: Complementary Reimagined
nodes.community_name: Optional Client Pack and Difficulty Map

nodes.community_name: Optional Client Pack and Difficulty Map

nodes.label: Sodium
nodes.community_name: Optional Client Pack and Difficulty Map

nodes.label: Xaero World Map Bridge
nodes.community_name: Optional Client Pack and Difficulty Map
nodes.rationale: Hook for Ark's colored danger overlay; NeoForge support is labelled experimental and its bytecode insertion descriptor matches exactly one invocation in Xaero's GuiMap renderer.

nodes.label: Xaero's World Map
nodes.community_name: Optional Client Pack and Difficulty Map
nodes.rationale: Pinned to 1.44.2 because the bridge's published compatibility matrix covers that series; keep the pair pinned until a later combination is checked.

nodes.label: River Redux
nodes.community_name: Optional Client Pack and Difficulty Map
nodes.rationale: No published 26.2 NeoForge artifact; do not install the older 1.21.x JAR or change Minecraft versions, and the land habitat planner works with ordinary exposed water blocks without its API.

nodes.label: TerraBlender
nodes.community_name: Optional Client Pack and Difficulty Map

nodes.label: Optional Client Pack and Difficulty Map
nodes.community_name: Optional Client Pack and Difficulty Map
nodes.norm_label: optional client pack and difficulty map
nodes.rationale: Presentation mods are client-only and managed by the extras installer; the standalone audio source mods must not be installed alongside Ark.

nodes.label: Dev-Run Dependencies and Settings
nodes.community_name: Optional Client Pack and Difficulty Map

nodes.label: Difficulty Map and Unlock
nodes.community_name: Optional Client Pack and Difficulty Map
nodes.rationale: Map temporarily open because progression.mapRequiresUnlock defaults to false; the intended milestone is taming a creature originating in a difficulty-5 region, and the entitlement is saved per player UUID.

nodes.label: Iris GL Validation Workaround
nodes.community_name: Optional Client Pack and Difficulty Map
nodes.rationale: The crash in GlCommandEncoder.validateDraw matches Iris issue 3304, so the interactive client run sets -Dneoforge.disableGlValidation=true; this does not patch Iris itself.

nodes.label: Install-Ark-Extras Installer
nodes.community_name: Optional Client Pack and Difficulty Map
nodes.rationale: Downloads fixed files from Modrinth's HTTPS CDN, verifies SHA-512 hashes and reuses matching files; it never overwrites changed files silently or modifies saves/configs.

nodes.label: Dev Runtime Properties (16 GB, 24 chunks)
nodes.community_name: Optional Client Pack and Difficulty Map
nodes.rationale: Client and dedicated-server heaps are 16 GB each (separate profiles, not combined), render/view distance is 24 chunks and simulation distance is 12, independently configurable.

nodes.label: DinoDebugSnapshot.capture
nodes.rationale: Extension point for computed values; mod-owned runtime fields are discovered automatically but taming/torpor lives in NeoForge data attachments so it is not shown as readable rows, and entity references appear as UUID/type rather than traversed.

nodes.label: TorporService
nodes.rationale: The only method that writes torpor is TorporService.sedate; tickEntity is the deterministic entry point used by game tests and sync calls Entity.syncData every torporSyncIntervalTicks while dirty.

nodes.label: TorporState Attachment
nodes.rationale: A NeoForge data attachment on any LivingEntity holding torpor, recovery delay, sedation phase and the sleeping-player anchor; there is intentionally no UUID-to-state map anywhere.

nodes.label: Debug Spyglass
nodes.rationale: A read-only inspector, not a variable editor; the server selects the closest visible living Ark creature intersecting the eye ray within 96 blocks and no survival recipe is added.

nodes.label: Code Inspection Report 2026-09-19
nodes.rationale: Full read of 101 feature files cross-checked against generated JSON and the game log; findings are listed only when verified in code and line numbers are current working-tree positions.

nodes.label: Debug Spyglass Page Budget
nodes.rationale: One 12-line page every 10 ticks keeps ordinary pages below 4 KiB, under 8 KiB/s per continuously active viewer; scans run only while the scope is in use and page requests are validated and rate-limited.

nodes.label: Defect: Debug Spyglass Ships in Production
nodes.norm_label: defect: debug spyglass ships in production
nodes.rationale: Item, creative-tab entry and server snapshot streamer register unconditionally with no config, permission or FMLEnvironment.isProduction() gate, exposing hidden creature state within 96 blocks on release servers.

nodes.label: Defect: Land think() Scan Cost
nodes.rationale: Each think() runs a large entity scan, up to 24 detect raycasts, a fluid/chunk probe and forage reads every 10 ticks, so cost scales quadratically with local population.

nodes.label: Defect: Mount Screen Labels Double Offset
nodes.norm_label: defect: mount screen labels double offset
nodes.rationale: extractLabels recomputes xo/yo inside a matrix already translated by leftPos/topPos, so Taming/Hunger/Torpor readouts draw near the bottom-right corner or outside the panel.

nodes.label: Defect: Tamed Creatures Keep Wild AI
nodes.norm_label: defect: tamed creatures keep wild ai
nodes.rationale: Critical: canUse() only checks alive and landHabitat while prey(other) is true for any player, so a ridden tame bites its own rider and a dismounted owner counts as an intruder, making taming actively harmful.

nodes.label: Defect: Titanosaur Cannot Satisfy SEEK_WATER
nodes.rationale: nearbyWater() scans at most 12 blocks while seekWater() places the destination 16 blocks back for a 30-block-wide Titanosaur, so it only finds water it cannot detect and never drinks.

nodes.label: Defect: Torpor Suppression Lost After Reload
nodes.norm_label: defect: torpor suppression lost after reload
nodes.rationale: installSuppression() is only called from sedate(), and goal selectors are rebuilt on reload, so a knocked-out vanilla mob resumes walking, targeting and attacking while the attachment still says TORPID.

nodes.label: Defect: Tranquilizer Arrow Recipe Never Loads
nodes.norm_label: defect: tranquilizer arrow recipe never loads
nodes.rationale: Datagen emits pre-1.21.5 ingredient syntax so the recipe fails codec parsing, removing the entire ranged sedative route; fix must regenerate through ArkData rather than hand-editing.

nodes.label: Defect: WildlifeNoise.hear Checks Before Distance Rejection
nodes.norm_label: defect: wildlifenoise.hear checks before distance rejection
nodes.rationale: Chunk-span loaded checks and raycasts run before the cheap distance test, so mining noise anywhere in the dimension causes per-creature scans and raycasts at a 10-tick cadence.

nodes.label: DimensionGuard
nodes.rationale: Refuses access without touching dimension ids, saved data or registry entries; players already inside a removed dimension return to safe Overworld ground on join and respawn.

nodes.label: LootGuard
nodes.rationale: Strips enchantment functions and removed items from parsed loot tables; tables holding built-in registry references cannot be re-encoded and are left untouched, and the server log reports those ids.

nodes.label: RecipeGuard
nodes.rationale: 53 recipes are removed as raw JSON before deserialization and the 8 copper bulb recipes are re-authored, so the removals cannot be bypassed by a data reload.

nodes.label: Self-Determination Theory Research
nodes.rationale: Autonomy, competence and relatedness linked to enjoyment, and expected tangible rewards can reduce intrinsic motivation; used as a framework for design, not proof of a recipe.

nodes.label: WHO Gaming Disorder Definition
nodes.rationale: Concerns impaired control, gaming priority over other activities and continuation despite harm with significant impairment; enjoying a long campaign alone does not establish the condition.

nodes.label: Survival Progression Roadmap
nodes.rationale: Prepared 20 September 2026 for a two-player cooperative campaign; it is a proposal, not implemented gameplay, and all durations and balance targets are design hypotheses to test.

nodes.label: Theme Alignment
nodes.rationale: The mod is a prehistoric survival experience and Minecraft's fantasy content competes for the same purpose as hunting, herding and reading terrain; everything is enforced twice because a saved level cannot be rewritten by a data pack.

nodes.label: Guardian Encounter Ladder
nodes.rationale: An early guardian teaches the combat grammar, three Mid regional guardians each test a different preparation problem, and a multi-phase apex finale with an explicit installation objective; visible windups and two-player scaling, and reward issuance must be idempotent across reloads.

nodes.label: Mod Integration Decisions
nodes.rationale: Keep 26.2 and build a compact native campaign; without verified 26.2 artifacts, defer Create, Farmer's Delight, Immersive Engineering and FTB Quests, and never infer compatibility from separately listed NeoForge and Minecraft versions.

nodes.label: Recovery Policy
nodes.rationale: Keep research and base ownership through death; dropped expedition gear goes into a persistent recoverable container with no item decay timer and a per-player cap, and base attacks stay opt-in rather than offline destruction retention pressure.

nodes.label: Four-Stage Campaign Architecture
nodes.rationale: Hand gathering, creature-assisted production, organized expeditions, industrial preparation and mastery encounters over a roughly 40-70 active-hour first clear; progress should change what you do, and a solved problem stops being repeated.

nodes.label: Shared Tribe Journal
nodes.rationale: Research is earned by discovering and using things rather than killing trivial animals; both players share unlocks and boss records while owned tames stay individually identifiable with explicit tribe permissions.

nodes.label: Fantasy Hostile Creature Removal
nodes.rationale: Removes zombies, skeletons, creepers, illagers, phantoms, guardians, piglins, wardens and constructed servants while keeping ordinary spiders, animals, villagers and every mod creature; an explicit /summon still works because administrator commands are not survival routes.

nodes.label: Grounded Material Sources
nodes.rationale: Bones come from animal carcasses (23 vanilla animals, 1-2 at 75%) so bone meal and wolf taming survive the skeletons; gunpowder and slime balls keep the wandering trader as their grounded source, and removed drops with no grounded role are removed rather than replaced.

nodes.label: LocomotionSignal Hysteresis
nodes.rationale: A 1.0 blocks/second start and three-tick 0.25 stop over measured travel; it deliberately ignores GeckoLib's render-state movement flag, which counts collision creep, pack jostle and sub-walking drift as travel.

nodes.label: Movement Tuning
nodes.rationale: Restart after editing the server config; damage and HP formulas are unchanged.

nodes.label: Ark Survival Returns README
nodes.rationale: A prehistoric wildlife mod for Minecraft Java 26.2, NeoForge 26.2.0.11-beta, Java 25 and GeckoLib 5.5.3 with mod id arksurvivalreturns; launch by double-clicking Start-Ark-Mod.bat.

nodes.label: Size, Speed and Body Scaling
nodes.rationale: Titanosaur 6x (30 x 42 blocks), Rex/Giga keep 3x and remaining species 2x; meshes, animation position tracks, collision bodies and eye heights scale together, and existing creatures adopt the new speed baseline without healing or rerolling levels.

nodes.label: Difficulty and Apex Correction
nodes.rationale: Replaced the capped radial distance that left all distant terrain at level 5; displayed rank is authoritative and regional large species treat the biome tag as a x3/x1 weight so an apex stays reachable wherever the rank admits it.

nodes.label: Species sprintRatio Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Each species exposes sprintRatio against the 5.612 blocks/second unbuffed player sprint benchmark; the ratio describes full pursuit/flee speed on unobstructed ordinary ground and player potion buffs do not change the benchmark.

nodes.label: strideScale Animation Cadence
nodes.rationale: Animation timing uses measured travel, body height and clip duration, so large bodies take slower longer strides at the same ground speed; increase strideScale to slow visual cadence without changing movement.

nodes.label: waterRetention Swimming Compensation
nodes.rationale: Swimming compensates for water drag while retaining collision, gravity and buoyancy; current paths, turning and currents still affect travel.

nodes.label: Berry Harvesting System
nodes.rationale: Breaking short or tall grass without shears has a 35% chance to drop 1-2 berries with weights 30/30/30/10; narcoberry is a sedative rather than taming food, and the upper half of tall grass does not make a second roll.

nodes.label: Five Recurring Danger Ranks
nodes.rationale: Ranks repeat in curved regions with about 20% of the area each and a 1,024-block period; the displayed rank is authoritative so a level-5 plains can spawn an apex while level 1 remains protected.

nodes.label: Level-Based HP and Damage Formulas
nodes.rationale: max HP = min(1024, base HP x (1 + 0.10 x n^0.85)) and melee damage = base damage x (1 + 0.14 x sqrt(n)); the 1024 ceiling respects Minecraft's health attribute limit and existing creatures keep saved stats without healing on reload.
